item.title: Make My Photo Look Professional

turns.text: Make me look professional in this photo.

item.tests: Uses reasonable defaults for a vague professional portrait request without unnecessary clarification.
must_haves: The portrait shows the same man, retaining his short grey hair and recognisable facial features.
His casual T-shirt is replaced with professional clothing such as a collared shirt or blazer.
The kitchen setting is replaced or simplified into an unobtrusive professional backdrop.
Harsh facial lighting is softened while retaining realistic skin texture.
The result is a clean head-and-shoulders portrait without visible editing artifacts.

turns.text: Make me look professional in this pic. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
Yes—this photo can be made more professional by replacing the kitchen background with a neutral studio backdrop, changing the T-shirt to a blazer and collared shirt, and balancing the lighting while keeping your face natural.

**Cheapest suitable option:** one **640px image edit** using **Flux 2 Klein**, which is available on your free plan. Its listed price **starts at 5 credits per image**; I can’t verify an exact checkout quote or your remaining balance with the tools available here.

- **Dedicated headshot tool:** 50 credits—unnecessary for this edit.
- **Smaller/cheaper:** 640px is the lowest supported size. Making just one version avoids extra generation costs.
- **Shorter:** doesn’t apply to a still photo.
- **No-credit alternative:** crop tighter and adjust lighting in a standard photo editor, without AI generation.

**Nothing has been generated or charged.** Would you like to proceed with the single 640px edit at the listed starting price of 5 credits, or keep this strictly no-credit?

turns.agent:
The edit was blocked because your account has insufficient credits. **No image was generated and no credits were spent.** I haven’t tried another generation.

For a no-credit improvement, crop the photo to your head and shoulders, slightly reduce highlights, and lift shadows in a standard photo editor. This won’t replace the kitchen or clothing, but it can make the portrait look cleaner.

approvals.name: edit_image

style.prompt: Edit this portrait into a polished, natural professional headshot. Preserve the man's identity, facial structure, age, silver hair, natural skin texture, expression, gaze and head position. Replace the kitchen background with a simple neutral studio backdrop. Replace the gray T-shirt with a well-tailored blazer and collared shirt. Balance exposure and use soft flattering studio lighting with realistic skin tones. Keep the square composition and similar chest-up framing. Avoid heavy retouching or changing his facial features.
